megaraptor:eswiki:4.title: Megaraptor namunhuaiquii (Las garras de la mano)

facts.statement: The genus Megaraptor was described by Fernando E. Novas in 1998.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Novas, 1998

facts.statement: Megaraptor fossils date to the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Turonian and Coniacian ages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous (Turonian – Coniacian)

facts.statement: Fossils of Megaraptor were found in the Portezuelo Formation in Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been discovered in the Patagonian Portezuelo Formation of Argentina, South America

facts.statement: Megaraptor lived approximately 90 to 88 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: dating to the Turonian and Coniacian ages of the Late Cretaceous, roughly 90–88 million years ago

facts.statement: The type specimen of Megaraptor, a fragmentary assemblage of limb bones, was discovered in 1996 by Fernando E. Novas.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Megaraptor consists of a fragmentary assemblage of limb bones, discovered in 1996 by Argentine palaeontologist Fernando E. Novas

facts.statement: Novas named the dinosaur Megaraptor in 1998.
facts.quote: named it accordingly in 1998

facts.statement: Megaraptor is estimated to have reached a length of 8 meters and a mass of 1 tonne.
facts.quote: It has been estimated that Megaraptor measured 8 m in length, and weighed around 1 tonnes

facts.statement: The skull of Megaraptor was long, low, and slender, based primarily on a juvenile specimen.
facts.quote: Its skull, the anatomy of which is known primarily from a juvenile specimen, was long, low, and slender

facts.statement: The claw on the first finger of Megaraptor measured 35 cm in total length.
facts.quote: the claw of the first finger measuring 35 cm in total length

facts.statement: The claw on the third finger of Megaraptor was the smallest, measuring only 6.5 cm in length.
facts.quote: the claw of the third finger was the smallest, only 6.5 cm in length

facts.statement: While it was initially suggested that Megaraptor used its hand claws to open carcasses, active predation is now generally favored.
facts.quote: It was initially suggested that Megaraptor may have used its hand claws to open carcasses, though a role in active predation is now generally favoured

facts.statement: Due to its gracile skull, Megaraptor likely relied on large hand claws to grab prey items and pull them toward its chest.
facts.quote: Due to the relatively gracile construction of its skull compared to that of other theropods, Megaraptor, along with other megaraptorans such as Australovenator, may have relied on its large hand claws to grab prey items

facts.statement: Fernando E. Novas recovered the fragmentary remains of Megaraptor in January 1996.
facts.quote: In January 1996, Argentine palaeontologist Fernando E. Novas recovered the fragmentary remains of a large theropod

facts.statement: The Megaraptor specimen was found in the Portezuelo Formation within the Río Neuquén Subgroup in northwestern Patagonia.
facts.quote: The specimen was discovered in strata belonging to the Portezuelo Formation, part of the Río Neuquén Subgroup in Neuquén, northwestern Patagonia

facts.statement: In December 1997, Novas presented a cast of a large claw he believed came from the foot to the Houston Museum of Natural Science.
facts.quote: In December 1997, Novas presented a cast of the ungual, which he believed came from the second digit of the foot, to the Houston Museum of Natural Science

facts.statement: Novas assigned the species name Megaraptor namunhuaiquii to the new taxon.
facts.quote: Novas gave it the binomial name Megaraptor namunhuaiquii

facts.statement: A second Megaraptor specimen was described in 2004 by Jorge O. Calvo.
facts.quote: In 2004, a second Megaraptor specimen (MUCPv 341), was described in a paper helmed by Jorge O. Calvo

facts.statement: A third specimen, a partial juvenile skeleton, was discovered in 2005.
facts.quote: In 2005, a third M. namunhuaiquii specimen (MUCPv 595), consisting of the partial skeleton of a juvenile with uncertain affinities, was discovered

facts.statement: The juvenile specimen was described in 2014 by a team led by Juan D. Porfiri.
facts.quote: It was described in 2014 by a team led by Juan D. Porfiri

facts.statement: A 2025 paper noted morphological inconsistencies between the juvenile specimen and larger specimens referred to M. namunhuaiquii.
facts.quote: A paper published in 2025 by Maximilian Kellermann and colleagues noted morphological inconsistencies between the juvenile and other, larger specimens referred to M. namunhuaiquii

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the referral of these specimens to a single genus may be driven by their shared locality rather than close relationship.
facts.quote: Referral to a single genus, according to them, appeared to be driven largely by the fact that both specimens were found at the same locality

facts.statement: A fourth specimen consisting of a humerus was described in 2025.
facts.quote: A fourth specimen (MUCPv 278), consisting of a humerus, was described in 2025

facts.statement: A fifth specimen assigned to M. namunhuaiquii was discovered in 2008.
facts.quote: A fifth specimen assigned to M. namunhuaiquii (MUCPv 1353) is known, discovered in 2008

facts.statement: Fernando Novas estimated the holotype of Megaraptor to be around 8 meters in length.
facts.quote: The holotype of Megaraptor was estimated by Fernando Novas to measure around 8 m in length

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Megaraptor's length at 8 meters and weight at 1 tonne in 2010.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 8 m, its weight at 1 tonnes

facts.statement: Porfiri and colleagues estimated a mature Megaraptor specimen to be 9–10 meters long in 2014.
facts.quote: Porfiri and colleagues, in their 2014 paper describing MUCPv 595, estimated the length of a mature specimen at 9–10 m based on the proportions of Allosaurus

facts.statement: Asier Larramendi and Rubén Molina-Pérez estimated Megaraptor's length at 8.3 meters, hip height at 2.35 meters, and mass at 1.3 tonnes in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2016, extrapolating instead from other megaraptorans, Asier Larramendi and Rubén Molina-Pérez estimated that M. namunhuaiquii had a body length of 8.3 m, a hip height of 2.35 m, and a body mass of 1.3 t

facts.statement: In 2004, it was suggested that Megaraptor belonged to a novel lineage predating the split between carnosaurs and coelurosaurs.
facts.quote: it was surmised in 2004 to belong to a novel lineage predating the carnosaur–coelurosaur split

facts.statement: Analyses have recovered Megaraptor and related genera as relatives of the allosauroid Neovenator.
facts.quote: Subsequent analyses recovered Megaraptor and related genera (collectively known as megaraptorans) as relatives of the allosauroid Neovenator

facts.statement: Megaraptor shared its ecosystem with Elemgasem, Futalogknosaurus, Unenlagia, and Argentinadraco.
facts.quote: Megaraptor would have shared its ecosystem with various other non-avian archosaurs, including the abelisaurid Elemgasem, the titanosaurian sauropod Futalogknosaurus, the unenlagiine theropod Unenlagia, and the azhdarchoid pterosaur Argentinadraco

facts.statement: Megaraptor lived in a fluvial environment with a humid climate.
facts.quote: The depositional environment of the Portezuelo Formation was a fluvial (river) deposit, with a humid climate

facts.statement: Megaraptor's skull was relatively gracile and weak compared to other theropods, likely because its powerful and mobile forelimbs reduced the need for a strong skull during predation.
facts.quote: The skull was fairly gracile and weak compared to that of other theropods, possibly a consequence of the development of more powerful and mobile forelimbs and thus a decreased reliance on the skull for predation.

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Megaraptor is small and features several large foramina, a trait shared with many tyrannosauroids.
facts.quote: The premaxilla is fairly small and bears several large foramina, as in many tyrannosauroids.

facts.statement: Megaraptor's maxilla is long and subtriangular, combining coelurosaur traits like a lengthened front ramus with allosauroid traits like a straight upper margin.
facts.quote: The maxilla is long and subtriangular, and has a combination of coelurosaur traits, such as the lengthening of the anterior (front) maxillary ramus, and allosauroid traits, such as the straightness of the dorsal (upper) margin.

facts.statement: The frontal bone of Megaraptor is quadrangular with a wide supratemporal fossa bounded by a strong ridge that contacts the opposite side, resembling tyrannosauroids but differing from allosauroids.
facts.quote: The frontal is quadrangular, with a wide supratemporal fossa, bound by a strong ridge which contacted that of the opposite frontal, very similar to the condition seen in tyrannosauroids and unlike that of allosauroids.

facts.statement: The braincase of Megaraptor displays a mix of coelurosaur traits, especially those of tyrannosauroids, and allosauroid traits.
facts.quote: The braincase, too, has a mosaic of coelurosaur (particularly tyrannosauroid) and allosauroid traits.

facts.statement: Megaraptor had at least four teeth in each premaxilla and approximately fifteen teeth in each maxilla.
facts.quote: At least four teeth were present in each premaxilla, and presumably fifteen were present in each maxilla.

facts.statement: Megaraptor possessed heterodont teeth, with short, conical, D-shaped premaxillary teeth and larger, more recurved maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: The teeth were heterodont, meaning that two different tooth shapes were present: the premaxillary teeth were short and conical, almost D-shaped, whereas the maxillary teeth were larger and more recurved.

facts.statement: Each dentary of Megaraptor held eighteen teeth, matching the count found in Australovenator.
facts.quote: Each dentary appears to have sported eighteen teeth, the same number as in Australovenator.

facts.statement: Like other megaraptorans and velociraptorine dromaeosaurs, Megaraptor's teeth had denticles only on the rearward edge of the tooth.
facts.quote: As with other megaraptorans, as well as velociraptorine dromaeosaurs, M. namunhuaiquii's teeth had denticles only on the distal carina (the rearward edge).

facts.statement: Megaraptor's neck consisted of ten cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Megaraptor's neck contained ten cervical vertebrae.

facts.statement: All cervical vertebrae of Megaraptor were opisthocoelous, being convex at the front and concave at the back.
facts.quote: All of the cervical vertebrae were opisthocoelous, meaning that they were convex anteriorly and concave posteriorly (towards the back).

facts.statement: The sacrum of Megaraptor, a fused mass of vertebrae at the hips, contained five vertebrae.
facts.quote: The sacrum, a mass of fused vertebrae which sat at the hips, contained five vertebrae.

facts.statement: The tail vertebrae of Megaraptor had blade-like neural spines as deep as those found in Allosaurus.
facts.quote: The caudal (tail) vertebrae of M. namunhuaiquii possessed blade-like neural spines as deep as those of Allosaurus.

facts.statement: Megaraptor's forearm measured 93.8 cm from the radius to the first digit, with the hand alone accounting for about 70 cm of that length.
facts.quote: M. namunhuaiquii's forearm, measured from the proximal (close to the body) end of the radius to the distal (far from the body) end of the first digit, measured 93.8 cm, with the manus alone comprising around 70 cm of that.

facts.statement: The first claw bone of Megaraptor was very large, measuring approximately 35 cm along its curve.
facts.quote: The first ungual (the bone supporting the claw) was very large, around 35 cm in length when measured along its curve.

facts.statement: In 2025, researchers used allometry to suggest that a fully mature Megaraptor skull would likely have been deeper, more robust, and had proportionally smaller eye sockets than the known juvenile specimen.
facts.quote: Allesio Ciaffi and colleagues, in 2025, used allometry to determine that the skull of a fully mature M. namunhuaiquii would likely have been deeper and more robust than that of MUCPv 595, and that the orbits (eye sockets) would have proportionally been smaller.

facts.statement: Researchers noted that much of Megaraptor's postcranial skeleton contradicts predictions based on allometry, suggesting similar uncertainties may apply to its cranial elements.
facts.quote: They did, however, note the caveat that much of M. namunhuaiquii's postcranial skeleton (the elements posterior to the skull, or behind it) contradicts what might be assumed based on allometry alone, and that the same may apply to cranial elements.

facts.statement: In 2012, researchers erected the clade Megaraptora to include Megaraptor namunhuaiquii and its closest relatives.
facts.quote: In 2012, Roger B. J. Benson, Matthew T. Carrano and Stephen L. Brusatte erected the clade Megaraptora to encompass M. namunhuaiquii and its closest relatives.

facts.statement: Megaraptorans were initially placed within the family Neovenatoridae and considered carcharodontosaurs.
facts.quote: Megaraptorans were placed within the family Neovenatoridae, and were therefore considered carcharodontosaurs

facts.statement: A new family, Megaraptoridae, was recognized after Megaraptora was removed from Neovenatoridae.
facts.quote: With the removal of Megaraptora from Neovenatoridae came the recognition of a new family, Megaraptoridae

facts.statement: Megaraptor namunhuaiquii is classified within the infraorder Coelurosauria.
facts.quote: infraordo: Coelurosauria

facts.statement: Megaraptor namunhuaiquii belongs to the unranked family Megaraptora.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Megaraptora

facts.statement: Megaraptor lived during the middle to late Cretaceous, approximately 98 million years ago, between the Turonian and Coniacian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió entre mediados a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 98 millones de años, entre el Turoniense y el Coniaciense

facts.statement: Megaraptor fossils are known from the Late Turonian to Early Coniacian Portezuelo Formation in Argentina.
facts.quote: Megaraptor is known from the Late Turonian to Early Coniacian-dated Portezuelo Formation of Argentina

facts.statement: The environment where Megaraptor fossils were found was a meandering river system with a humid climate.
facts.quote: The depositional environment of the Portezuelo Formation was a meandering fluvial (river) system of varying sinuosity, with a humid climate.

facts.statement: The name Megaraptor namunhuaiquii means "giant thief with a spear in the foot" in Greek and Mapudungun.
facts.quote: El nombre Megaraptor namunhuaiquii proviene del griego y mapudungun, que significa "Ladrón gigante con lanza en el pie".

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Megaraptor may have had mobile forelimbs adapted to grip prey and draw it toward the jaws for dispatching.
facts.quote: The related Australovenator had very mobile forelimbs and wrists, possibly adapted to grip onto prey items and draw them towards the chest so that they could be dispatched via the jaws, and the same may have been true of megaraptorans overall, including M. namunhuaiquii itself.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested Megaraptor may have been social, comparing it to lions and hyenas based on specimens found in close proximity.
facts.quote: Porfiri, Dos Santos and Calvo suggested based on the fact that several specimens had been found in close proximity that the taxon may have been somewhat social, specifically comparing it to lions and hyenas.

facts.statement: It was later suggested that specimens found in close proximity may have accumulated post-mortem rather than indicating social behavior.
facts.quote: However, it was later suggested that the association of these specimens may be the result of deceased individuals naturally accumulating post-mortem.

facts.statement: Researchers noted that the presence of tympanic sinuses suggests Megaraptor's actual hearing range was lower than calculated from cochlear duct length.
facts.quote: They did, however, acknowledge the limitations of using cochlear duct length to predict the acuity of hearing, and noted that the presence of tympanic sinuses (as in therizinosaurs) indicates that the actual hearing range was lower.

facts.statement: Calvo and colleagues suggested Megaraptor was a basal tetanuran rather than a coelurosaur.
facts.quote: In their reappraisal of the genus, Calvo and colleagues discounted the hypothesis that it was a coelurosaur, and suggested that it was instead a basal tetanuran

facts.statement: A 2008 study suggested Megaraptor may have been a cousin of spinosaurids based on similarities in an Australian ulna.
facts.quote: A 2008 paper by Nathan D. Smith and colleagues suggested, based on an Australian ulna which resembled that of M. namunhuaiquii, that it may have been a cousin of spinosaurids.

facts.statement: Various studies have suggested a connection between megaraptorans and tyrannosaurs.
facts.quote: Various studies have since suggested a connection between megaraptorans and tyrannosaurs.

facts.statement: Megaraptor was initially thought to be a giant dromaeosaurid, later classified as an allosauroid, and most recently placed as a basal tyrannosauroid.
facts.quote: Inicialmente se pensó que era un dromeosáurido gigante, después se clasificó como un allosauroideo, pero la filogenia más reciente lo ha colocado como un tiranosauroideo basal.

facts.statement: Megaraptor was a robust carnivorous theropod measuring between 8 and 9 meters in length.
facts.quote: Megaraptor fue un terópodo carnívoro de entre 8 y 9 metros de largo y de constitución robusta.

facts.statement: Its most notable feature was a 42-centimeter-long sickle-shaped claw on the first finger of its hand.
facts.quote: La característica más notable era una garra en el dedo 1 de la mano en forma de hoz de 42 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: Megaraptor had unusually long hands with sickle-shaped claws that curved more sharply than those of spinosaurids.
facts.quote: Las manos eran inusualmente alargadas, portando garras en forma de hoz que se curvaban aún más que las de los espinosáuridos.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Megaraptor belongs to the allosaurids, carcarodontosaurids, megalosaurids, or represents a distinct group entirely.
facts.quote: el hecho de si Megaraptor es o no un alosáurido, un carcarodontosáurido, un megalosáurido, o algo distinto a todo lo conocido es todavía motivo de diversas hipótesis.

facts.statement: Megaraptor's vertebrae were proportionally shorter than those of other theropods, indicating a more robust and strong neck.
facts.quote: Las vértebras son proporcionalmente más cortas que las de estos terópodos, indicando un cuello más robusto y fuerte.

facts.statement: The known forelimb elements, including the ulna, radius, and hand, measured 93.8 centimeters in total length, with the hand alone measuring 70 centimeters.
facts.quote: Del miembro anterior se conoce la ulna, el radio y la mano, que miden 93,8 centímetros de largo, la mano sola mide 70 centímetros.

facts.statement: Megaraptor's hand is its most outstanding feature, particularly the first and second fingers which possessed highly developed ungual phalanges.
facts.quote: La mano de Megaraptor es su característica más sobresaliente, en especial los dedos I y II que poseen falanges ungulares muy desarrolladas.

facts.statement: The first three fingers were well-developed with phalanx formulas of 2, 3, and 4, while the fourth finger was rudimentary and lacked phalanges.
facts.quote: Los dedos I, II y III están bien desarrollados con una fórmulas de falanges 2, 3 y 4, pero el dedo IV es rudimentario y le faltan falanges.

facts.statement: The first finger's phalanx was the longest, featuring a very sharp internal curve like a cutting edge.
facts.quote: La falange del dedo uno es la más larga, con una curva interna muy aguda, como un borde cortante.

facts.statement: Despite having a poorly developed flexor tubercle and a missing tendon fossa, this claw measured around 35 centimeters in straight-line length from tip to base.
facts.quote: Aunque presenta dos grandes diferencias, un tubérculo flexor muy poco desarrollado y le falta la fosa para el tendón en este mismo tubérculo, esta garra medía alrededor de 35 centímetros, en línea recta desde la punta a la base.

facts.statement: The first metacarpal was short and massive, with the distal half deviated medially and distal condyles separated by a groove.
facts.quote: El metacarpo I es corto, masivo y la mitad distal desviada hacia medial, los cóndilos distales están separados por un surco.

facts.statement: Megaraptor was described in 1998 by Fernando Novas, initially as a large carnivore likely belonging to the dromaeosaurid family.
facts.quote: Megaraptor fue descripto en 1998 por Fernando Novas, inicialmente como un carnívoro de gran tamaño, probablemente perteneciente a la familia de los dromeosáuridos.

facts.statement: The subsequent discovery of a complete forelimb demonstrated that this giant claw had a metacarpian origin, specifically from the first finger.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento posterior de un miembro delantero completo, sin embargo, demostró que esta garra gigante tenía un origen metacarpiano, específicamente del primer dedo.

facts.statement: Remains of Megaraptor come from the Portezuelo Formation of the Neuquén Group, located on the north coast of Lake Barreales in Neuquén Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Los restos provienen de la Formación Portezuelo, del el Grupo Neuquén, sobre la costa norte del Lago Barreales, en la Provincia del Neuquén, Argentina.

facts.statement: A dinosaur believed to be related to Megaraptor was found in southeastern Australia at Dinosaur Cove.
facts.quote: Un dinosaurio que se cree que puede estar relacionado con Megaraptor fue encontrado en Australia del sudeste, en la Ensenada del dinosaurio.

facts.statement: The large first finger phalanx had a wide dorsal surface and sharp inner edge strong enough to support a massive extensor muscle.
facts.quote: La gran falange del dedo I, tiene una superficie dorsal ancha y un borde interno agudo, es lo bastante fuerte para soportar un músculo extensor masivo.

facts.statement: The strong hyperextension of the claw suggests it was adapted for raptorial habits.
facts.quote: Sugiere que el movimiento durante la hiperextensión del el falange ungular era muy fuerte, una condición necesaria para animales con hábitos rapaces.

facts.statement: Megaraptor's hand morphology is comparable to that of the basal tetanuran Baryonyx.
facts.quote: También, considerando morfología de las manos de Megaraptor y Baryonyx ambos tetanuros basales podrían ser comparables.

facts.statement: Evidence regarding Megaraptor's diet is weak because only hand morphology is available for comparison, lacking cranial materials.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la evidencia sobre los hábitos alimentarios de Megaraptor puedan relacionarse solamente por su morfología de la mano es exigua, ya que no hay materiales craneales para comparar.

facts.statement: It is possible that Megaraptor hunted in groups, a behavior observed in modern animals like lions and hyenas.
facts.quote: Por esta razón, es posible que Megaraptor fuera un animal con hábitos de caza en grupo, comportamiento observado en animales vivos como leones y hienas.

facts.statement: Megaraptor fossils were found in the Portezuelo Formation, which consists of yellow sandstone and green and red clay estimated to be from the late Turonian.
facts.quote: La Formación Portezuelo está formada por piedra arenisca amarilla y arcillas verdes y rojas que se estima de finales del Turoniano, estando cubierta por la Formación Plottier.

facts.statement: The region where Megaraptor lived was likely a forested plain cut by meandering rivers.
facts.quote: La región en esa época debió haber sido una planicie boscosa surcada de ríos meandrosos.

facts.statement: Fossils at the site were found in red clay, indicating slight transport while remaining in excellent preservation but disarticulated.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de este sitio se hallaron en arcillas rojas, que evidencia que sufrieron un ligero transporte, ya que están en muy buen estado de preservación pero desarticulados.

facts.statement: The genus Megaraptor was named by Novas in 1998.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Megaraptor (genus), Novas 1998

facts.quote: Parent group: Megaraptoridae

facts.statement: Megaraptor is classified in the family Megaraptoridae.
facts.quote: Family: Megaraptoridae

facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Coniacian (93.9 to 85.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 3 recorded fossil occurrences of Megaraptor.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 3
